subject: Ceasefire, reopening of the strait, and reflection on cost
place: Strait of Hormuz, Geneva diplomatic conference
grounding_notes: Resolve the main arcs without declaring victory; the world is scarred and the peace is conditional.

included_characters.role_in_chapter: Executive Officer of the USS Truxtun
Civilian master of the Orion Pride

quality_parameters.philosophical_depth: explore the illusion of control and the distance between decision-makers and sufferers
quality_parameters.metaphorical_richness: use sea, gate, fire, and machine imagery consistently
quality_parameters.accessibility: clear to adult thriller readers without military background
quality_parameters.timelessness: echo classical questions of responsibility and mercy

chapter_summary: In a Geneva archive years later, the Archivist hands the Young Correspondent a sunrise photograph taken from the Truxtun on the morning the strait reopened, and charges her to write the story not as a chronicle of fleets but as a record of the people who held the line, made the mercy choice, and survived the narrow gate. The seed must return to the frame narrative, close the thematic arc on the illusion of control, and leave the reader with the image of a single tanker escorted by wary warships into a changed world.
theme: the price of reopening a broken world: no winners, only survivors
